messages:
jen: Hey team — multiple customers (two orgs) reporting intermittent 502s and stalled streaming responses to the hosted /v1/chat/stream endpoint since ~09:10 UTC. Customers see partial chunks then stream stops and client gets 502 or 504 depending on client timeout.

jen: Attaching quick repro from one customer: they open long-lived HTTP/2 streams, send a couple of messages, then expect model tokens streamed for ~20-30s. Failures usually after ~10-25s into the stream.

jen: Quick logs I pulled from our edge for one trace id: 
```
edge-log: env@edge-07 svc=envoy trace=trace-id-cc123 status=502 upstream_reset: code=REFUSED_STREAM details=upstream reset during body
edge-log: envoy: HTTP/2 GOAWAY last_stream_id=123 error_code=NO_ERROR debug=idle_timeout
```

sam: @jen thanks. Do we have upstream (model) traces? looking for backend latency spikes or OOMs.

jen: yes, grabbed traces from model-backend-2 for the same trace-id: 
```
backend: request_id=trace-id-cc123 recv=09:11:12 start_inference=09:11:14 heavy-kernel-swap=09:11:20 cpu% spike to 95% for ~6s rpc_send=09:11:26
```

raj: hmm looks like inference backend CPU spiking + longer token generation times. For streaming, Envoy keeps the h2 stream open waiting, and upstream delays cause envoys to hit keepalive/stream limits and issue GOAWAY or RST_STREAM. Could be connection pool exhaustion + concurrent stream limit on upstream.

maya: I'm seeing a correlated pattern in metrics: cluster.edge->model-upstream rq_active spiking, http2 concurrent streams at ~102 (our default max concurrent streams is 100), and prefix cache eviction events right before spikes. If prefix cache misses, token latency jumps.

jen: customer env: high-concurrency streaming (dozens of clients, each opens persistent h2). They also use function calls + large system prompts.

maya: Repro steps I used in staging:
1) run k6 script that opens 40 concurrent h2 streams with keepalive, each sends 2 messages and waits for streamed tokens for 30s.
2) disable prefix cache on model to simulate heavy backend work.
3) observe env logs: GOAWAY and RST_STREAM after backlog grows.

maya: k6 snippet:
```
// pseudo k6: open 40 h2 clients, each:
const client = new httpx.Client({http2: true});
client.post('https://api.redwood.dev/v1/chat/stream', { body: payload, headers });
```

sam: Good repro. Two potential fault domains: (A) upstream model latency from cache misses/quantization GC causing long blocking; (B) Envoy/edge connection limits + h2 keepalive semantics dropping streams when new stream attempts exceed last_stream_id or max_concurrent_streams.

raj: Logs show envoy set 'goaway' with debug idle_timeout in one cluster and REFUSED_STREAM in another. REFUSED_STREAM typically when upstream treated stream as transiently not accepted (eg, connection exhausted).

jen: Customers are asking for mitigation asap. Any short-term mitigations we can apply at edge?

sam: Short term: increase http2 max_concurrent_streams on envoy->upstream to 200 and bump max_connections in cluster config; increase upstream idle_timeout and stream_idle_timeout. Also enable prioritization of existing streams (if feature flagged) so new heavy requests don't starve streaming.

maya: Also can add a temporary routing rule: route requests with header `x-client-streaming: long` to a dedicated pool with higher concurrency (or to dedicated capacity for that customer if available).

raj: For hosted customers we can also throttle concurrent streams per API key to avoid head-of-line. Implement per-key concurrency quota (soft limit) as emergency control.

jen: Do we want me to open a deploy to bump max_concurrent_streams on edge clusters now? @deploy-bot what is the risk?

deploy-bot: Automated: config change to envoy clusters requires rolling restart of edge proxies in region-us-east-1. Risk: brief increase in connection churn during restarts, usually safe with 30s stagger.

sam: ok do it but staged: apply to a single POP first (edge-07 where these traces originated) and monitor 1 hour. Add increased logging for h2 stream events and track REFUSED_STREAM and GOAWAY counts.

jen: I'll kickoff a canary rollout to edge-07 now (config bump max_concurrent_streams=250, max_connections=2000, stream_idle_timeout=60s).

infra-bot: config-change: canary apply started for cluster=edge-pop-07 by jen at 09:37 UTC.

maya: Also pushing a quick fix on model side: lower prefix cache eviction aggressiveness and patch the quantized runtime to prefetch KV ranges for active prompts to avoid cache miss storm. Deploying a build to model-backend-2 for test.

raj: Post-mitigation checklist:
- monitor streaming success rate (target >99%)
- watch CPU on model-backend (should stabilize)
- trace counts of GOAWAY/REFUSED_STREAM down to baseline
- confirm customers can complete 30s streams without resets

jen: After canary (10m) we saw GOAWAY events drop ~80% on edge-07 and customer reported improved success for 2 test streams. I'll proceed to roll to other POPs, one at a time.

maya: Model patch in staging reduced median token latency from 220ms -> 90ms on those long prompts. That's promising.

sam: Next steps (medium term):
- add per-api-key streaming concurrency throttles on control plane
- add explicit streaming pool in routing and config presets for customers that need long-lived h2 sessions
- surface a recommended config in docs for heavy-streaming workloads (prompt size, batching, concurrency)

jen: FYI support note to customers sent: short description of mitigation and suggestion to try a reduced system prompt size and to add `x-client-streaming: long` header if they want us to route to the streaming-optimized pool (while we expose it).

jen: I'll keep thread updated as we roll. thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-sre for follow-ups on autoscaling and upstream connection handling.

infra-bot: config-change: canary apply completed on edge-pop-07 at 09:48 UTC. No crashes, 2% connection churn observed during restart window.

jen: Last check: after full roll to remaining POPs yesterday, customer streams stable for 48h and support tickets closed. Marking this resolved, will open a follow-up ticket for per-key throttles and streaming pool roadmap.

sam: good wrap.

jen: closing thread.
